title: C-type natriuretic peptide and natriuretic peptide receptor B signalling inhibits cardiac sympathetic neurotransmission and autonomic function
central_claims: CNP acting through NPR-B reduces calcium signaling and norepinephrine release in cardiac sympathetic neurons.
Impaired neuronal CNP/NPR-B signaling produces sympathoexcitation, hypertension, tachycardia and reduced ventricular systolic function in transgenic rats.

source_manifest.title: C-type natriuretic peptide and natriuretic peptide receptor B signalling inhibits cardiac sympathetic neurotransmission and autonomic function
source_manifest.finding: Rat neuronal NPR-B inhibition and acute CNP experiments support a sympathoinhibitory mechanism; central action, dose and causal direction remain limitations.

source_manifest.title: C-type natriuretic peptide (CNP) in the paraventricular nucleus-mediated renal sympatho-inhibition
source_manifest.finding: Independent PVN experiments extend the sympathoinhibitory question to renal output and central neurons, explicitly citing the stellate-neuron finding. NPR-C is implicated; NPR-B involvement is not excluded.

source_manifest.title: C-Type Natriuretic Peptide in Essential Hypertension: Old Ways for a New Time
source_manifest.finding: Independent perspective retains neuronal NPR-B inhibition of calcium and norepinephrine release and the transgenic-rat hypertension finding, while stressing animal evidence and uncertain therapeutic translation.

source_manifest.title: C-type natriuretic peptide co-ordinates cardiac structure and function
source_manifest.finding: Cardiomyocyte/fibroblast protection depends chiefly on NPR-C in these models. This tissue-specific result limits broad NPR-B cardioprotection claims but does not retest neuronal sympathetic transmission.

research.summary: The neuronal finding persists in independent synthesis and a later central-sympathetic investigation. Matched replication and clinical translation remain unverified; distinct NPR-C effects in heart muscle are not treated as confirmation or refutation of neuronal NPR-B.
